description: The quintessential Indian Sign Language greeting and welcome. The human instructor joins both open flat palms smoothly at chest level in a respectful prayer/Namaste posture with a gentle forward head tilt and warm welcoming smile.
steps: Raise both hands to mid-chest height with open flat palms facing one another.
Bring palms and fingers together smoothly at the sternum in a Namaste posture.
Gently tilt head forward with a warm, respectful facial expression.

components.movement: Hands meet at midline with slight forward extension
components.expression: Warm smile, polite forward head bow

cultural_note: In ISL, Namaste is both an informal 'hello' and a formal mark of respect when meeting elders, guests, and community members.

description: Universal expression of gratitude in Indian Sign Language. The human instructor touches fingertips of dominant open flat hand to chin/lower lip, then sweeps forward and slightly downward toward the viewer with an appreciative nod.
steps: Place the fingertips of your dominant flat hand lightly against your chin or lower lip.
Glide your hand smoothly forward and slightly downward toward the person you are thanking.
Nod your head affirmatively with a grateful, polite facial expression.

components.location: Chin / Lower Lip to Forward Signing Space
components.movement: Forward and downward arc toward listener

cultural_note: Used universally across Indian deaf communities to express appreciation, relief, and polite closure.

description: The fundamental wellness inquiry. The human signer holds closed fists with thumbs pointing upward at chest height, twists wrists outward so palms face up, followed by pointing the index finger forward toward the person with questioning raised eyebrows.
steps: Hold both hands as closed fists with thumbs pointing upward at chest height.
Rotate wrists outward so thumbs roll forward and palms face upward.
Point dominant index finger forward toward the person with raised, inquiring eyebrows.

components.handshape: Thumbs-Up Fists transitioning to Index Point
components.expression: Inquisitive raised eyebrows, slight head tilt

cultural_note: Facial grammar is critical in ISL questions: raised eyebrows signal a yes/no or open wellness inquiry.

english: I am fine / I am good
description: The standard optimistic response to wellness inquiries. The signer taps their dominant index finger to the chest to indicate 'I / Me', followed by presenting a solid, firm thumbs-up moving forward with an affirmative head nod.
steps: Point your dominant index finger toward your chest to indicate 'I / Me'.
Form a clean thumbs-up with dominant hand, thumb extended firmly upward.
Move the thumbs-up hand slightly forward and upward with a confident, cheerful nod.

components.movement: Self-referential point followed by positive push

cultural_note: A strong thumbs-up with a head nod communicates good health, confidence, and readiness to interact.

description: Essential introductory question. The human instructor points index finger forward toward the person ('YOU'), taps extended index and middle fingers crosswise twice ('NAME'), then extends open upturned palms with inquisitive facial grammar ('WHAT').
steps: Point index finger forward at the listener ('YOU').
Extend index and middle fingers on both hands and tap them crosswise twice ('NAME').
Turn both palms face up and spread hands slightly outward with raised brows ('WHAT?').

components.handshape: Index Point -> Two-Finger 'H' Cross-Tap -> Open Upturned Palms
components.location: Neutral Signing Space in front of torso
components.movement: Point -> Cross tap -> Upward palm open
components.expression: Inquisitive furrowed or raised eyebrows, forward chin

cultural_note: ISL follows topic-comment word order (YOU NAME WHAT?), placing the question word at the end.

description: Essential sentence for introducing yourself. The signer places a flat open palm gently over the center of the chest ('MY'), taps index and middle fingers crosswise twice ('NAME'), then fingerspells the letters of their name.
steps: Place flat open palm gently on the center of your chest ('MY').
Bring index and middle fingers together on both hands and tap them crosswise twice ('NAME').
Spell out the letters of your name using the 26 ISL manual alphabets.

components.movement: Chest press -> Double tap -> Sequential letters

cultural_note: After fingerspelling their name, Deaf signers in India often share a unique 'Sign Name' given by the community.

description: Polite greeting conclusion. The dominant open palm slides smoothly across the flat non-dominant palm ('NICE/GOOD'), both index fingers held upright converge together in front of the body until they touch ('MEET'), then point to the person ('YOU').
steps: Glide dominant open flat palm smoothly across non-dominant palm ('NICE / GOOD').
Hold both index fingers straight up pointing toward ceiling and bring them together until knuckles touch ('MEET').
Point index finger gently toward the other person ('YOU').
cultural_note: The two converging index fingers visually symbolize two individuals walking toward each other and meeting.

instructor: Goa Board of Education ISL Signer
description: Indispensable emergency and assistance sentence. Non-dominant hand flat, palm facing up; dominant hand forms closed fist with thumb upright resting atop non-dominant palm. Lift both hands together moving inward toward chest with earnest expression.
steps: Extend non-dominant hand flat with palm facing upward as a supportive platform.
Place dominant hand in a thumb-up fist directly onto the flat palm ('HELP').
Lift both hands simultaneously moving them inward toward yourself ('HELP ME').

components.location: Lower Torso moving upward and inward to Chest
components.expression: Earnest, pleading or urgent facial expression

cultural_note: Moving the combined hands inward means 'help me'; moving them outward toward the other person means 'I help you'.

description: Crucial daily practical sentence. The human signer forms a 'T' or 'W' handshape with dominant hand, gently shaking side-to-side twice from the wrist ('TOILET/WASHROOM'), followed by turning both palms up with questioning look ('WHERE').
steps: Form a 'T' handshape (thumb protruding between index and middle finger knuckles).
Gently shake the hand back and forth from the wrist twice ('TOILET / RESTROOM').
Open both hands with palms facing upward and shoulders slightly shrugged ('WHERE?').

components.location: Shoulder height to Lower Rib level

cultural_note: Universally recognized in public transport, colleges, and workplaces across India.

description: Standard daytime greeting and parting sentence in ISL. Touch chin with flat fingertips and bring forward ('GOOD'), then raise dominant hand up from horizontal non-dominant arm like sunrise ('MORNING') / wave open palm followed by 'V' shape from eyes forward ('SEE YOU AGAIN').
steps: Touch fingers to chin and push forward ('GOOD').
Rest non-dominant forearm horizontally while dominant hand rises up behind it like sunrise ('MORNING').
Form 'V' (two fingers) pointing outward from eyes and wave hand smoothly ('SEE YOU AGAIN / BYE').

components.handshape: Flat Palm (Good) -> Sunrise Rise -> 'V' Sight Direction
components.location: Chin to Chest to Eye level
components.movement: Chin outward -> Vertical rise -> Outward look wave
components.expression: Bright cheerful smile, direct eye contact

cultural_note: A polite, positive closure honoring the visual bond between signers.
